title: View: China has resolved its ‘Malacca Dilemma’
gist: Andy Browne argues the Iran war energy shock showed China has escaped its 'Malacca Dilemma' through stockpiles, overland pipelines, coal-to-chemicals and green tech, while energy-importing US allies Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines struggle. That reverses the logic of a US oil blockade and coincides with stepped-up Chinese grey-zone pressure and no US carriers in the Indo-Pacific.

insights.claim: China's economy survived the Iran war oil supply disruption largely unscathed thanks to large oil stockpiles, overland pipelines, coal-to-chemicals technologies and green technology adoption.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Lowers the perceived economic cost to China of energy shocks and blockade threats, changing Asia risk calculus.
insights.quote: Not only has China’s economy survived the oil supply disruption largely unscathed
insights.locator: The war in Iran has shattered those assumptions

insights.claim: For at least 25 years, US strategists assumed the US Navy could cripple China's economy as a last resort by blocking the Strait of Malacca, through which most of China's seaborne oil imports pass, and the Iran war has shattered that assumption.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Weakens a core US deterrent lever, potentially emboldening Chinese pressure on Taiwan.
insights.quote: The war in Iran has shattered those assumptions.

insights.claim: Hu Jintao's 2003 'Malacca Dilemma' concern has driven Beijing's industrial, military and diplomatic strategy, with the Belt & Road Initiative largely a defensive move to reduce exposure to US maritime threats.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Explains China's long-term investment in Eurasian overland energy and trade routes.

insights.claim: Hoover fellow Eyck Freymann argues a US blockade of China would now hurt US allies more than China.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Energy-importing Asian allies are the more vulnerable economies in any blockade scenario.
insights.quote: “You’d starve out your allies before you starve out China,”

themes.theme: US allies squeezed by energy shock

insights.claim: Island economies around China, including Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines, are struggling because they rely overwhelmingly on imported energy.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Energy-importing Asian economies carry higher macro and currency risk while the Iran war persists.
insights.locator: The war in Iran has shattered those assumptions

insights.claim: The Trump administration faces growing economic and political fallout from rising inflation caused by the energy shock.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Energy-driven inflation adds pressure on US policy and the domestic political calendar.

themes.theme: Grey-zone pressure and US force posture

insights.claim: China has intensified grey-zone intimidation as the Iran war drags on, including more coast guard patrols off Taiwan's east coast to assert law-enforcement control over shipping routes and stepped-up claims in Philippine waters.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Raises shipping and geopolitical risk premia around Taiwan and the South China Sea.
insights.locator: Chinese coast guard vessels have increased patrols

insights.claim: Japan, dependent on open sea lanes, has been alarmed by Chinese moves and is in a spat with China over remarks by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi about Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Japan-China tensions are a live risk factor for Japanese equities and trade.

insights.claim: For the first time in decades, the US 7th Fleet has no aircraft carriers operating in the Indo-Pacific, as the Iran war strains the carrier force and exposes US Asia-Pacific bases within easy reach of Chinese missiles.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: A US naval gap in Asia raises the window of opportunity for Chinese coercion.
insights.quote: For the first time in decades, the US 7th Fleet has no carriers operating in the Indo-Pacific.

insights.claim: The view that striking Iran delivers a devastating blow to China, Iran's main oil customer, is wrong according to Browne, since China has built multiple routes to escape an energy blockade and turned the tables on Washington.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Investors should not assume the Iran war weakens China's strategic position.

insights.claim: A former Indian ambassador writes that the likelihood of the Strait of Malacca being monetized or weaponized is growing, spurring bypass projects such as a new land bridge in Thailand.
insights.speaker: Andy Browne
insights.so_what: Chokepoint-bypass infrastructure in Southeast Asia could attract investment.
insights.quote: “the likelihood of Malacca being monetized and, if necessary, weaponized, appears to be growing,”
